A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DrMMD research, with matching authors, method, main theorems and original experiments. Their complete text, equations, figures and appendices support comparison; v2 adds Appendix C.

before.justification: Section 8 and Figures 1–2 report original three-ring particle-flow experiments and student–teacher network training results.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original Gaussian particle-descent diagnostics in Appendix C and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The DrMMD functional, regularized kernel, adaptive regularization schedule and particle updates in Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Appendix C uses Gaussian projection for illustrative analysis without changing the proposed particle algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds a direct one-dimensional Gaussian matching scenario, initialized at N(0,3) with target N(0,6). The three-ring and student–teacher tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The three-ring comparison retains MMD, KALE and locally estimated χ² descent. The student–teacher comparison retains MMD and DrMMD with and without noise injection. Appendix C introduces no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The new Gaussian experiment uses 10,000 particles, step size 0.01, and evaluates KL divergence and density-ratio derivative norms. The existing Section 8 sample sizes, training settings and evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a focused empirical examination of regularity quantities underlying the convergence assumptions. Figure 3 tracks these quantities during particle descent without Gaussian projection; v1 contains no corresponding diagnostic.

E5.justification: Appendix C adds Gaussian kernel-density estimation with lengthscale 0.1 for density-based diagnostics and reports particle-estimated KL. This introduces an estimation procedure, but adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 3 newly reports overall decreases in estimated KL and both regularity diagnostics during the Gaussian experiment. Figures 1–2 retain their original plotted results and comparative conclusions; their resizing does not indicate performance changes.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds substantial formal analysis: Gaussian moment dynamics, Hermite spectral calculations, range-condition and regularity bounds, and Lemmas C.1–C.2 with proofs. Variance monotonicity is proved for the limiting χ² and MMD regimes but remains conjectural for general positive regularization. The existing main convergence theorems are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central contributions: tractable sample-based DrMMD flow, near-global convergence guarantees, and adaptive regularization balancing approximation and discretization errors.

C2.justification: Remark 5.3 replaces the earlier log-Sobolev-based LMC comparison with a Poincaré-based comparison and explains DrMMD's additional approximation error. New discussion clarifies practical tuning, limitations of finite-particle bounds, image-generation extensions and the conditional nature of Appendix C's Gaussian analysis.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new Gaussian simulation and density-estimation settings. Section 6 also clarifies that theoretical step-size constants are generally unavailable and step sizes are selected for empirical convergence. The existing experimental settings and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: New Section 7.2 substantially develops the relationship to diffusion models. Expanded discussions address mollifier-based flows, alternative spectral regularization and newer finite-particle analyses, including Banerjee et al. and Chen et al. Appendix C adds supporting literature on Gaussian flows and spectral calculations.

P1.justification: V2 makes widespread small copyedits, expands selected explanatory passages, adds Section 7.2 and Appendix C, and introduces additional proof subheadings. The original narrative and main section order remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The JMLR formatting changes the title and author block, running headers, spacing and figure placement. Figures 1–2 are resized with their content preserved, and Figure 3 adds one diagnostic plot.

improvement.justification: Appendix C's worked example and particle diagnostics make the regularity assumptions more concrete, while the expanded comparisons and tuning discussion clarify applicability. These improve exposition and supporting evidence, but general positive-regularization monotonicity remains conjectural, and the main guarantees and original experiments are unchanged. The added theoretical support therefore remains limited.
